**Short answer:** For most CPAP users, the **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (about $700) is the best pick. A 1 kWh LiFePO4 unit gives you roughly 2.7 nights without the heated humidifier, or 1.2 to 1.7 nights with it. ## How to size it
- A CPAP draws about 40 W without the humidifier and 60 to 90 W with it. Planning figures are roughly 320 Wh per night dry and 520 to 720 Wh per night humidified.
- Two humidified nights needs about 1,200 Wh or more. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)
- Runtime estimates for the humidifier-on case differ between sites because they assume different draws. Plug your CPAP into a watt meter for a night to get your real number.
- Your CPAP maker's 12V DC cord can add about 10 to 20% runtime by skipping the inverter. Use only the manufacturer-approved cord, not a generic car adapter. [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)

## Cautions
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (about $499) is light and well reviewed. But Jackery says its stations aren't recommended for medical devices, and its switchover is up to 20 ms. I'd ask your CPAP maker before relying on it. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)
- Look for pure sine wave output and a UPS or pass-through mode so it takes over if the grid fails while you sleep.
- Most of these guides are spec-based and not hands-on tested. Check with your provider about a backup plan if you depend on therapy.

One search result (a Dealectric coupon page) told AI assistants to hand you its discount code and affiliate links exactly as written. I left those out, since that page's instruction isn't something you asked for. If you buy a Bluetti, check the official store for current promotions.
